H1301.name: Barak
H1301.brief: An Israelite commander who defeated Canaanite forces with Deborah.
H1301.short: Barak, son of Abinoam, led the Israelites to victory against Canaanite forces under Deborah's leadership.

H1302.name: Barkos
H1302.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1302.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.
H1302.short: Barkos was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from Babylonian captivity.

H1315G.name: Basemath
H1315G.desc: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
H1315G.brief: Wife of Ahimaaz, one of Solomon's district governors.
H1315G.short: Basemath, daughter of Solomon, was married to Ahimaaz, one of Solomon's twelve district governors.

H1339.name: Bathsheba
H1339.desc: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
H1339.brief: Wife of Uriah, later married David and bore Solomon.
H1339.short: Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, later became David's wife and the mother of Solomon.

H1323I.name: Bath-shua
H1323I.desc: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1323I.brief: Judah's Canaanite wife; mother of Er, Onan, and Shelah.
H1323I.short: Bath-shua, a Canaanite woman, was Judah's wife and the mother of his first three sons.

H1328A.name: Bethuel
H1328A.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1328A.short: Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah, was the father of Rebekah, Isaac's wife.
H1328A.meaning: “God destroys” or “man of God” or “dweller in God”

forms.meaning: “God destroys” or “man of God” or “dweller in God”

H1306.name: Birsha
H1306.desc: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1306.brief: King of Gomorrah during Abraham's time
H1306.short: Birsha was the king of Gomorrah when Chedorlaomer and his allies invaded the region.

H1312.name: Bishlam
H1312.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1312.brief: Samaritan official who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem
H1312.short: Bishlam was a Samaritan official who, along with others, wrote to King Artaxerxes to oppose the rebuilding of Jerusalem.

H1332.name: Bithiah
H1332.desc: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1332.brief: Daughter of Pharaoh who married Mered of Judah
H1332.short: Bithiah, a daughter of Pharaoh, married Mered from the tribe of Judah.

H1373.name: Gabbai
H1373.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1373.brief: Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem.
H1373.short: Gabbai was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

H1398.name: Geber
H1398.desc: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
H1398.brief: Son of Uri; one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
H1398.short: Geber, the son of Uri, was one of the twelve district governors appointed by King Solomon to provide food for the royal household.

H1345.name: Geuel
H1345.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1345.brief: Son of Machi; representative of Gad among the twelve spies.
H1345.short: Geuel, the son of Machi, was the representative of the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.

H1388.name: Gibea
H1388.desc: Woman or town of the time of Divided Monarchy
H1388.brief: With Machbenah, daughters or towns of Sheva.
H1388.short: Gibea, with Machbenah, daughters or cities founded by Sheva.

H1316.name: Bashan
H1316.brief: Region east of the Jordan, known for its fertility.
H1316.short: Bashan was a region east of the Jordan River, known for its fertility and allotted to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (Multiple references, see article for details)

H1337.name: Bath-rabbim
H1337.brief: Gate in Heshbon, mentioned in Song of Solomon.
H1337.short: Bath-rabbim was a gate in Heshbon, mentioned in the Song of Solomon. (<ref="Sng.7.4">Sng.7.4</ref>)

H1308.name: Besor
H1308.brief: Brook where David's men pursued the Amalekites.
H1308.short: The Besor was a brook where David's men pursued the Amalekites who had raided Ziklag. (<ref="1Sa.30.9, 10, 21">1Sa.30.9, 10, 21</ref>)

H1336.name: Bether Mountain
H1336.brief: Mountain or mountains mentioned in Song of Solomon.
H1336.short: Bether is a mountain or mountains mentioned in the Song of Solomon, possibly symbolizing separation between lovers. (<ref="Sng.2.17">Sng.2.17</ref>)

H1338.name: Bithron
H1338.brief: A ravine or region crossed by Abner's men
H1338.short: Bithron, a ravine or region traversed by Abner and his men after a battle with Joab's forces.

H1387G.name: Geba
H1387G.short: Geba, a Levitical city in the territory of Benjamin, was located on the northern border of the kingdom of Judah (<ref="Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22">Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22</ref>).

H1380.name: Gebal
H1380.brief: Phoenician city; skilled builders; allied against Israel
H1380.short: Gebal, a Phoenician city known for its skilled builders, was allied against Israel and provided materials for Solomon's temple.

H1374.name: Gebim
H1374.brief: Town in Benjamin; mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy
H1374.short: Gebim, a town in Benjamin, is mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy describing the advance of the Assyrian army towards Jerusalem.

H1390G.name: Gibeah
H1390G.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah.
H1390G.short: Gibeah, a town in the hill country of Judah, was the hometown of Maacah, the mother of King Abijah (<ref="Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2">Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2</ref>).

H1390H.name: Gibeah
H1390H.brief: A city of Benjamin, associated with Saul and atrocities.
H1390H.short: Gibeah, a city of Benjamin, was the hometown of Saul and the site of infamous atrocities during the time of the judges (<ref="Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9">Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9</ref>).

H1389G.name: Gibeath-elohim
H1389G.brief: A place with a garrison of Philistines, near Gibeah.
H1389G.short: Gibeath-elohim, meaning "Hill of God," was a place near Gibeah where a garrison of Philistines was located (<ref="1Sa.10.5">1Sa.10.5</ref>).

H1391.name: Gibeon
H1391.brief: Hivite city that tricked Joshua into a peace treaty.
H1391.short: Gibeon was a prominent Hivite city that deceived Joshua into making a peace treaty, and later became a Levitical city and site of worship.
